D008-D018_h001.question:
I… I don’t know when it starts or stops anymore. For about a month last spring, I’d go days on three hours of sleep and still feel like I was buzzing. My thoughts raced so fast I couldn’t finish sentences—like ten ideas exploding at once, none of them mine, all demanding to be written down. I’d walk in circles around my apartment, editing the same paragraph over and over, convinced it had to be perfect, but I couldn’t focus long enough to fix it. Small things—like a neighbor’s music or my phone pinging—would set me off. I snapped at my editor, said things I regret. I didn’t feel manic—I felt urgent, like if I stopped moving, I’d collapse.

Then it flipped. For two months, I couldn’t get off the couch. Writing felt pointless. I’d stare at the blank screen like it was judging me. I stopped returning calls. Even showering took too much energy. I kept thinking… what’s the point? I’ve been through stuff—bad stuff, years ago—but I never let it define me. Lately, though, I wonder if it’s all catching up. Or if I’m just broken. Some days I’m wired again, others I can’t breathe under the weight. I don’t know which version is real.
D008-D018_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D008-D018_h001.answer: C & D. Bipolar I Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D008-D018_h002.question:

I drag myself out of bed, exhausted no matter how long I sleep. I keep thinking I’ve failed them somehow—like that parent conference last week was my fault, even though nothing went wrong. I even apologized to my principal for “not doing enough,” which makes no sense, but it feels true. I’ve missed planning days, forgotten emails. My brain just won’t stay still when it’s buzzing, or won’t move at all when it’s stuck. I don’t know what’s wrong with me.

D008-D018_h003.question:

D008-D018_h004.question:

D008-D018_h007.question:

I’ll redesign entire branding concepts in one night and barely notice I haven’t slept. I don’t *feel* tired, so I don’t see the point in stopping. My coworkers say I’ve been snapping over little things—a pen clicking, someone humming—and I hate that I can’t control it. 

There are flashes, though… moments when a smell or a sound hits me wrong, and I’m back in that parking garage last winter. I try not to think about it. But sometimes, I’ll just *freeze*, or get this intense rush like I need to run, even if I’m just at my desk. I don’t know if it’s connected, really. I mean, the not sleeping and the irritability—they come and go. They don’t always line up with the memories. 

I keep trying to work through it, but my focus bounces. A fan spinning, a notification chime—my attention just lurches toward it. I can’t explain it. Part of me wonders if it’s just burnout, or if something else is going on. It’s not every day, but when it hits, it’s hard to function.

D008-D018_h008.question:

But it’s not like I’m happy about anything specific—it just sort of bubbles up.

I don’t know when sleep became optional. I’ll lie down at ten, maybe drift off for an hour or two, but then I’m up—cleaning out drawers, writing letters to old friends I haven’t thought of in decades. Once I drove to the next town at 3 a.m. just to buy a new hat. Felt sharp, awake, like my thoughts are sprinting ahead. But then I lose track—start writing that letter and suddenly I’m folding laundry, then watering plants, then staring at the wall wondering where the hour went.

There’s this restlessness, like I can’t sit still even when I’m tired—which I don’t feel, really. I suppose part of this might have something to do with the war—sometimes images pop in, not full memories, just flashes. My wife used to say I’d twitch in my sleep. But I don’t know if that’s connected. It’s all just… here now. Hard to slow down. Hard to explain.
D008-D018_h008.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
D008-D018_h008.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D008-D018_h011.question:

I can’t focus, can’t push through tasks I used to do easily. Deadlines are piling up. Part of me thinks, *Maybe I just won’t wake up one day.* I don’t want to hurt myself, but the thought crosses my mind when it all feels pointless.

Something happened a while back—something bad—I don’t really talk about it. But I can’t tell if that’s connected, or if I’m just… broken in some other way.

D008-D018_h022.question:
Lately… it’s been like I’m at war with myself. For a couple of months last year, I felt unstoppable—jacked up, like I’d had ten coffees. I wasn’t tired, didn’t need sleep, just kept moving. Felt like I had some big idea burning inside me, but if you ask me what it was? I can’t say. Don’t remember. I maxed out two credit cards—tools, a truck I didn’t need, bought my wife a boat. She still hasn’t forgiven me.  

Then it crashed. Three months of just… nothing. Didn’t want to go to work, didn’t fish, didn’t touch the grill. My head’s foggy—I’m forgetting orders, where I left my keys. Waking up at 3 a.m., heart racing, just staring at the ceiling. I’ve thought… well, if the press fails, or there’s an accident, it’d be cleaner just to not be here. Thought about the old service revolver in the closet. When. Where. How.  

Look, twenty years in the shop, you see things. Bad burns, near-misses. Can’t say one was *worse* than another. But I don’t dream about them. Not really. Just… the not sleeping. The jumpiness. Comes and goes. Can’t pin it on anything specific.

D008-D018_h023.question:

D008-D018_h024.question:
I’ve been going through… something. For about two months, I felt like I couldn’t stop—I was dancing longer, faster, pushing past exhaustion like it wasn’t real. I wasn’t tired. I’d change choreography in the middle of rehearsal, convinced I’d invented something brilliant. My mood? I felt electric, like I was glowing. I bought so many things—leotards, pointe shoes, even a designer bag I couldn’t afford—just because I *needed* them in that moment.

I lie in bed for hours, unable to fall asleep, just staring. My thoughts are thick, slow—like trying to swim with weights on. Sometimes, standing on the rooftop during smoke breaks, I get this sudden rush—just *jump*—but I don’t plan it. It’s just there.  

Something happened last year… I don’t like to talk about it. Was it related? I don’t know. The highs and lows don’t seem tied to anything specific. They just come.
